clue.text: Millions start of revolution purged from Russia in conflict once

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

indicators.note: something purged is cleared out, so the named letter is taken away from the following word

parts.note: the old Soviet Union, Russia's former state

indicators.note: 'start of' keeps only the first letter of 'revolution'

parts.note: the opening letter of revolution

explanation.surface: A historical note: millions died as the revolution began and purges swept Soviet Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia' stands for the old Soviet state's initials. The answer is an obsolete sense, a scramble or disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records muss as an obsolete word for a scramble or squabble, hence a conflict of former times.

clue.text: Brewery vessel, bottom up, with wood, over half of it, inside

parts.note: slang for the bottom

indicators.note: half of means only one of the two letters is kept

parts.note: one half, the second letter, of it

explanation.surface: A brewery vat turned upside down, with wooden staves over half of it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mash tub is the vessel in which malt is steeped in hot water during brewing.

clue.text: It's a famous dame, sprightly character but not lead in panto

indicators.note: but not means a letter is excluded from the preceding word

parts.note: a spark is a lively person
the leading letter of panto

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame who is lively, yet not the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dame' suggests pantomime; it is the Dame of Sark, the island's hereditary ruler, notably Dame Sibyl Hathaway. Sark is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is famous for its feudal ruler, the Dame, so it is the place that 'has' a famous dame.

clue.text: Garden species producing small branch, say, climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say

explanation.surface: A garden plant that puts out a small branch, a climbing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge, genus Euphorbia, is a large group of plants, many grown in gardens.

clue.text: Rustic pair of lads holding post in festival excitement

parts.note: two sons

explanation.walkthrough: The post sits between the two sons.

clue.text: Give severe ticking-off to timid creature when last in subject

parts.note: final letter of subject

clue.text: Idle fellow, once with line on river

explanation.surface: An idle man of old sitting fishing with a line on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusk is an obsolete word for a lazy lout or sluggard.

clue.text: Develop as in classical verses poet hammers out about love

love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical verses' alludes to Ovid's Metamorphoses, poems about transformations.
explanation.definitionFit: To metamorphose is to change form, as the figures in Ovid's poem are transformed.

clue.text: A pair of drums got up in sort of silver

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Second string holding contest up? It records performance

clue.text: Head up old copper completes beat as of old

clue.text: A page publisher inserted on one side in the main, spread with various printing inks (9, three words)

taken as written

Oxford University Press

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the open sea, so 'on one side in the main' is a nautical term for the sheltered side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: À la poupée is an intaglio printing method where several coloured inks are dabbed onto one plate with a rag doll (poupée).

clue.text: Prison get-up in theatre

the middle letter, P the abbreviation for page
love is nil, the letter O

clue.text: What shows black unit at last being given pride of place?

explanation.walkthrough: B + ONE makes BONE; its last letter moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for ebony or black, the stuff or colour that shows black.

clue.text: Specialist mathematician rooting around with with me shortened semester?

parts.note: anagram fodder

clue.text: One's labelled 'coarse', right out of gutter

clue.text: Height below rod, or 6 cubits for some

explanation.definitionFit: The caneh is a Hebrew unit of length equal to six cubits, used by some ancient peoples.

clue.text: Catching cold, OAP shivers — I've fine wool coat

explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person as the animal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Paco is another name for the alpaca, the animal whose coat gives fine wool.

clue.text: Like telly (monstrous!) somebody was watching

eyed means looked at, watched

clue.text: Hot? Not very, with day ending
